verses.1: Then, after some time, King Yudhājit of Kekaya sent his own preceptor, Gārgya, the son of Angiras, a Brahmarshi of immeasurable splendor, to the great-souled Rama.
verses.2: And ten thousand horses, an unsurpassed gift of affection, were also sent.
verses.3: The king also gave blankets, jewels, excellent colorful garments, and auspicious ornaments to Rama.
verses.4: The intelligent Rama, having heard that the great sage Gargya, sent by his maternal uncle Ashvapati with great wealth, had arrived.
verses.5: And Rama, along with his younger brothers, went forth for a krosa to meet Gargya and honored him greatly, just as Indra honors Brihaspati.
verses.6: Having thus greatly honored that sage, received the wealth, and inquired about every detail of his maternal uncle's welfare, Rama then began to question the highly fortunate sage who was now seated.
verses.7: Rama asked what message his maternal uncle had sent, for which purpose the revered sage, who is the best among those skilled in speech, had arrived here, as if Brihaspati himself.
verses.8: Having heard Rama's words, the great sage began to narrate the detailed and wonderful matter to Rama.
verses.9: Yudhājit, your maternal uncle, O mighty-armed Rama, has spoken words filled with affection, which you should hear if they please you.
verses.10: This region of the Gandharvas, adorned with fruits and roots, lies on both banks of the Sindhu river and is exceedingly beautiful.
verses.11: O hero, that region is protected by three crores of very powerful Gandharvas, the sons of Shailūṣa, who are armed and skilled in warfare.
verses.12: O mighty-armed Rama, descendant of Kakutstha, having conquered those Gandharvas, establish your own well-governed and auspicious city in that Gandharva region.
verses.13: No one else has access to that exceedingly beautiful region; O mighty-armed one, may this proposal please you, for I would never speak anything harmful to you.
verses.14: Hearing the proposal from the great sage and his maternal uncle, Rama, pleased, agreed and then looked at Bharata.
verses.15: Pleased, Rama, with folded hands, said to the Brahmarshi Valmiki, "O Brahmarshi, these two princes will go forth to that region."
verses.16: These are Bharata's valiant sons, Taksha and Pushkala, who are well-protected by their maternal uncle and well-trained in righteousness.
verses.17: With Bharata leading, the two princes, accompanied by an army, will kill the sons of the Gandharvas and then establish two cities.
verses.18: Having established those excellent cities and settled his sons there, the very righteous Bharata will return to my presence again.
verses.19: Having thus spoken to the Brahmarshi Vashistha, Rama then commanded Bharata, who was accompanied by his army and followers, and consecrated the two princes.
verses.20: Bharata, honoring Vashistha (the son of Angiras) and choosing an auspicious constellation, set out with his army and the two princes.
verses.21: That army, as if accompanied by Indra, then departed far from the city, following Bharata, and was unconquerable even by the gods.
verses.22: Indeed, flesh-eating creatures and very great Rakshasas followed Bharata, driven by a thirst for blood.
verses.23: And many thousands of very terrible flesh-eating spirits, desirous of consuming the flesh of the Gandharva princes, also followed.
verses.24: Many thousands of lions, tigers, boars, and various birds marched in front of the army.
verses.25: After staying on the road for one and a half months, the army, healthy and filled with joyful and well-nourished people, arrived in Kekaya. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे शततमः सर्गः ।। 100 ।। Thus ends the hundredth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
